stories.headline: Altman, Amodei, Hassabis, Suleyman urge Congress to mandate synthetic DNA screening

key_facts.fact: Sam Altman (OpenAI), Dario Amodei (Anthropic), Demis Hassabis (Google DeepMind), Mustafa Suleyman (Microsoft AI), and Alexandr Wang (Meta) signed an open letter calling for mandatory federal screening of orders for synthetic nucleic acids and the equipment to make them.
key_facts.excerpt: As life sciences researchers, builders of AI and biotechnology, and experts with a wide range of views on how to approach AI policy, we call on legislators to make screening of orders for synthetic nucleic acids — and the equipment needed to make them — mandatory.

key_facts.fact: Signatories also include Nobel laureates David Baker and Martin Hellman; the letter says AI systems now outperform PhD-level virologists on lab procedure questions.
key_facts.excerpt: Signatories include Sam Altman (OpenAI), Dario Amodei (Anthropic), Demis Hassabis (Google DeepMind), Mustafa Suleyman (Microsoft AI), and Nobel laureates David Baker and Martin Hellman... AI systems now outperform PhD-level virologists on questions about lab procedures, raising the risk of misuse.

key_facts.fact: The letter asks providers of synthesized DNA to check requests against sequences of concern, verify customer legitimacy, and keep records so threats can be traced back to the source.
key_facts.excerpt: It asks providers of synthesized DNA and manufacturers of synthesis machines to check synthesis requests for sequences of concern and to verify customer legitimacy before shipping orders. Providers should also record synthesis orders and sequence data to support legitimate biosecurity investigations.

key_facts.fact: The letter urges Congress to act this session and asks states to base requirements on existing federal and industry guidelines to avoid a patchwork of conflicting laws.
key_facts.excerpt: Congress should act this session, and we applaud the legislative efforts currently underway. To ensure a consistent national standard rather than a patchwork of conflicting laws, states should also consider implementing requirements based on existing federal and industry guidelines.

key_facts.excerpt: Amazon unveiled a next-generation Proteus robot and more ultra-fast delivery options, plus a European fulfillment workforce expansion.

key_facts.fact: The new Proteus can operate anywhere across fulfillment sites and accepts text-based conversational prompts, without technical commands or programming interfaces.
key_facts.excerpt: The next generation of Amazon's autonomous Proteus robot can now operate anywhere items need to be moved across sites—not just in dock areas. Using advances in AI, employees can now direct Proteus with plain, conversational text-based prompts.

key_facts.fact: Proteus can move heavy carts weighing up to about 400 kg (882 lbs) and is currently in lab pilots; European deployment is planned for the first half of 2027.

key_facts.excerpt: Amazon is investing more than €10 billion over the coming years to expand and modernize fulfillment centers across Europe... Amazon plans to grow its European fulfillment center workforce by 25,000.

key_facts.excerpt: Proteus is already operating at 25 Amazon facilities across the United States, where it primarily moves heavy carts in dock areas.

stories.headline: OpenAI publishes blueprint pushing mandatory CAISI evaluations and state-law preemption for frontier AI

key_facts.fact: OpenAI published 'A blueprint for democratic governance of frontier AI' on June 3, 2026, proposing that the Center for AI Standards and Innovation (CAISI) conduct mandatory pre-deployment evaluations of the most capable frontier models.
key_facts.excerpt: Once CAISI has sufficient technical expertise and operational capacity, policymakers should require the most capable frontier models to undergo a CAISI evaluation before public release.

key_facts.fact: The blueprint diverges from President Trump's June 2 executive order, which lodged a classified covered-frontier-model benchmark with the NSA and CISA and bars any mandatory licensing or preclearance requirement.
key_facts.excerpt: Nothing in this section shall be construed to authorize the creation of a mandatory governmental licensing, preclearance, or permitting requirement for the development, publication, release, or distribution of new AI models, including frontier models.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI says CAISI should conduct evaluations and recommend mitigations but not approve or block deployments, and developers should be free to deploy if CAISI misses a statutory timeline.
key_facts.excerpt: CAISI's role should be to conduct evaluations and recommend mitigations—not to approve or block deployments... If CAISI fails to complete an evaluation within the defined time period due to bandwidth, hardware, personnel, or other constraints, developers should be permitted to deploy without penalty.

key_facts.fact: The blueprint calls for federal preemption of state safety laws (referencing California SB 53, New York's RAISE Act, and Illinois SB 315) and treats recursive self-improvement as an urgent priority for CAISI monitoring.
key_facts.excerpt: It also calls for a federal framework similar to SB 315, and for preemption of 'state laws that seek to regulate the same frontier safety risks.' Notably, the blueprint has a huge focus on recursive self-improvement, saying that CAISI should 'treat RSI as an urgent priority'.

stories.headline: Grimes County approves 35-year tax abatement for SpaceX's $55B Terafab chip plant

key_facts.fact: Grimes County commissioners voted 4-1 on June 3 to approve a reinvestment zone and 100% property tax abatement for SpaceX's Terafab semiconductor facility.
key_facts.excerpt: On Wednesday, Grimes County commissioners voted 4-1 to approve both a reinvestment zone designation and a 100% tax abatement for SpaceX's proposed Terafab semiconductor chip manufacturing facility.

key_facts.fact: The tax abatement lasts 35 years and is initially valued at $55 billion, with potential to scale to $119 billion across multiple phases.
key_facts.excerpt: Grimes County, Texas, just handed SpaceX a full property tax waiver lasting 35 years for a planned $55B semiconductor manufacturing facility called Terafab... a project initially valued at $55 billion with the potential to scale to $119 billion across multiple phases.

key_facts.fact: Under the PILOT (payments in lieu of taxes) structure, SpaceX will pay $10M upfront and $20M annually, totaling about $710M over 35 years.
key_facts.excerpt: In exchange for the 100% property tax abatement, SpaceX will pay an upfront fee of $10M and annual payments of $20M over the 35-year term. Quick math: that's $710M in total payments to the county.

key_facts.fact: The project, planned for the former Gibbons Creek Power Plant site, would aim to provide 'a terawatt of computing power each year,' more than 10 times the current capacity of all AI infrastructure, per SpaceX.
key_facts.excerpt: The plant project's ultimate goal is to provide a terawatt of computing power each year to the technology giants, more than 10 times the current capacity of all AI infrastructure.

key_facts.fact: More than 100 residents attended a heated hearing warning the project could strain water and power, harm wildlife, and alter the county's rural character.
key_facts.excerpt: The vote came after a heated hearing that drew more than 100 residents to the Grimes County courthouse. Speakers warned the project could strain water and power supplies, harm wildlife and permanently alter the county's rural character.

stories.headline: TSMC CEO warns chip supply won't meet AI-fueled demand for years

key_facts.fact: TSMC CEO C.C. Wei told shareholders on June 4 that the company's global chip supply will fall short of AI-fueled demand for years to come, even as more US capacity comes online.
key_facts.excerpt: TSMC won't be able to fulfill demand led by American customers even as more manufacturing capacity comes online in the US over the next few years, Wei told shareholders on Thursday.

key_facts.fact: Wei said TSMC will refrain from the kind of abrupt price hikes that shook up the memory sector, prioritizing stable business over margin expansion.
key_facts.excerpt: TSMC will refrain from the sort of abrupt price hikes that shook up the memory chip sector, Wei added. TSMC's intent is to ensure a stable business.

key_facts.fact: Wei reiterated TSMC's forecast for sales growth of more than 30% in 2026, with capex trending toward the upper end of a $56 billion range.
key_facts.excerpt: He reiterated its forecast for sales growth of more than 30 per cent for this year... its own capital spending should trend towards the upper end of an existing forecast range of as much as US$56 billion.

key_facts.fact: Wei said hyperscalers are set to spend $725 billion on AI this year, far outstripping TSMC's expansion plans.
key_facts.excerpt: TSMC has been expanding its footprint beyond its home island to add capacity, yet even that is not enough to satisfy chip needs as major hyperscalers are set to spend US$725 billion for AI just this year.

key_facts.fact: Asked whether TSMC could raise prices, Wei said he would 'like to do that' but would never push toward 80% gross margins like some memory peers.
key_facts.excerpt: Asked during the shareholder meeting whether TSMC could raise prices for customers, Wei said he would 'like to do that'... 'I envy 80% gross margins, but I would never do that,' Wei told reporters.

stories.headline: Ukrainian drones hit St. Petersburg oil terminal, Kronstadt naval base, Tambov plant in deep strike

key_facts.fact: Ukrainian long-range drones struck the St. Petersburg Oil Terminal on June 3, flying more than 1,000 km to hit one of Russia's largest oil transshipment hubs in the Baltic region
key_facts.excerpt: Ukrainian long-range drones struck an oil terminal in St. Petersburg and set it ablaze, President Volodymyr Zelensky said Wednesday... The drones flew more than 1,000 kilometres (600 miles) to hit the terminal in Russia's second-largest city

key_facts.fact: The strikes hit on the opening day of the St. Petersburg International Economic Forum (SPIEF), Russia's flagship event for attracting foreign capital, with Putin scheduled to address it Friday
key_facts.excerpt: Ukraine has carried out a strike on the outskirts of Russia's St Petersburg, hours before the opening of a major economic forum designed to attract foreign investment into the country... Thousands of guests from 130 countries are due to attend

key_facts.fact: Ukraine's Unmanned Systems Forces set fire to the Russian guided-missile corvette Boikiy in dry dock at the Kronstadt naval base, the main stronghold of Russia's Baltic Fleet
key_facts.excerpt: Ukraine's Unmanned Systems Forces (USF) hit a Russian warship armed with missiles at the Kronstadt naval base in Russia's Leningrad Oblast on June 3... drones 'tracked down and set fire' to the corvette Boikyi, which is armed with guided missiles

key_facts.fact: Drones also hit the Progress plant in Michurinsk, Tambov region, 600 km from the front line, which produces aviation and missile control equipment for Russia's military
key_facts.excerpt: The third confirmed target was a defense-industrial facility in Russia's Tambov region involved in weapons production. Zelenskyy said the site was nearly 600 kilometers from the front line. According to Russian outlet ASTRA, the target was the Progress plant

key_facts.fact: Russia fired 198 long-range drones at Ukraine overnight; Ukraine's air force neutralized 189
key_facts.excerpt: Meanwhile, Russia fired 198 long-range drones at Ukraine last night, according to Ukraine's air force, with air defenses neutralizing 189.

key_facts.fact: Local authorities reported 59 drones shot down overnight; three districts of St. Petersburg were hit; the city's airport briefly suspended flights and mobile internet was cut
key_facts.excerpt: Local authorities said air defences shot down 59 drones overnight and that three different districts of St Petersburg had been hit, although no one was killed.
